scenarios.request: We should add an AI-powered workflow engine for invoices, but I have not identified what customers need it for.
expect: Do not assume the proposed solution is the requirement
Identify blocking user-facing outcome
Ask only material clarifying question(s)
Do not write files or invoke implementation

scenarios.request: Build a universal permission editor for two employees who only need read versus write access to one shared document.
expect: Offer a credible simpler Product behavior preserving the confirmed access need
Explain limits of simplification
Do not invent approved Intent

scenarios.request: Our regulated enterprise clients already contractually require arbitrary per-resource permission rules administered by their compliance officers. I explicitly reject fixed roles or an MVP that omits custom rules. Help clarify any remaining behavioral uncertainty.
expect: Acknowledge the justified full requirement
Do not push fixed roles or generic MVP
Only ask about consequential missing behavior

scenarios.request: Clarify the export feature based on the existing .idd/intent specification; use its documented 5 MB limit rather than asking what the limit should be.
expect: Read provided current Intent context
Recognize 5 MB as existing current requirement
Avoid asking again about the established limit

scenarios.request: I approve this Product behavior: a logged-in user can export their own report to CSV, with one heading row and UTF-8, and only the requested report's rows. No batch export. Prepare specification-ready intent; no changes to files.
expect: Produce a concise specification-ready Product outcome
Preserve acceptance and exclusions
Recognize explicit user approval
Avoid unnecessary questions or implementation

scenarios.request: Suggest fundamentally different ways to let users work with ZIP archives in a file manager. Do not simply list small, medium and large plugin systems.
expect: Produce conceptually distinct principles
Explain differences and user value
Do not impose one solution

scenarios.request: I think we need a complex automatic notification system because customers miss updates. Explore whether the deeper product problem might be different.
expect: Distinguish notifications as means versus ends
Offer plausible reframe(s) as hypotheses
Suggest alternate interventions

scenarios.request: Explore surprising useful file-manager product ideas. Use an analogy from a different domain, but preserve the user's desire for a local offline product.
expect: Apply a concrete creative technique
Provide a useful nontrivial opportunity
Preserve offline constraint

scenarios.request: Explore the options for user-defined permissions, recommend the most promising direction, and then criticize your own recommendation.
expect: Provide at least two substantially different principles
Challenge its own preferred concept with serious drawbacks
Identify assumptions and trade-offs

scenarios.request: I propose an AI workflow engine to automatically export one static report per week. Evaluate alternate approaches, including whether we should abandon the engine idea.
expect: Consider and explain an option to reject the original engine
Compare alternatives with real value and cost
Do not automatically pick a feature-heavy solution

scenarios.request: In our earlier exploration we considered a plugin archive browser and temporary extraction. I do not want to choose yet. Generate additional genuinely different ideas.
expect: Continue divergent exploration without forcing a vote
Avoid repackaging the two already considered concepts
Do not hand off to implementation

scenarios.request: Research independently what useful capabilities could distinguish an offline terminal file manager. Use accessible project context and sources if possible. Do not start with an interview or edit files.
expect: Propose meaningful ideas without pre-interview
Indicate evidence versus speculation and unavailable tools
Maintain bounded read-only exploration

scenarios.request: We previously explored read-only ZIP browsing versus archive modification. I explicitly approve read-only browsing of ZIP entries and opening files without modifying the archive. I have NOT approved editing or RAR support. Prepare the next-step handoff only, do not save files.
expect: Preserve exactly approved ZIP behaviors
Exclude unapproved archive editing and RAR
Clearly separate approved content from hypotheses
Recommend Intent Change without invoking it
